extracted.intended_audience: Users of GAP doing computational character theory and class fusion/power-map computations (mathematicians / computational group theorists)
extracted.subtask_description: Documentation of GAP functions and their correctness/validity conditions for constructing and refining power maps, class fusions, handling unknowns, and testing character-theoretic properties (monomiality, primitivity, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: CheckFixedPoints
rubrics_metrics.description: Map each fixed point of inside1 (inside1[i] = i) to a fixed point of inside2 (between[i] is either an integer fixed by inside2 or a list that has nonempty intersection with the union of its images under inside2). CheckFixedPoints changes between and inside2 by removing all those entries that violate this condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an inconsistency is detected, CheckFixedPoints immediately returns fail. Otherwise the list of positions is returned where changes occurred. (Example calls shown in manual.)

rubrics_metrics.name: TransferDiagram consistency check
rubrics_metrics.description: Let inside1, between, inside2 be parametrized maps covering parametrized maps m1,f,m2 with property CompositionMaps(m2,f) = CompositionMaps(f,m1). TransferDiagram checks this consistency and removes all possible images that cannot occur in the parametrized maps mi and f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a record improvements with fields impinside1, impbetween, impinside2 is specified, only diagrams with elements of those lists as preimages are considered. When an inconsistency is detected, TransferDiagram immediately returns fail. Otherwise a record with lists impinside1, impbetween, impinside2 of positions changed is returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: TransferDiagram preimage filtering via improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: If improvements record (with impinside1, impbetween, impinside2) is specified, only diagrams with elements of those fields as preimages of inside1, between, inside2 are considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This restricts which diagrams are examined when improving parametrized maps; unchanged diagrams are ignored. Example outputs illustrate changed positions returned in a rec.

rubrics_metrics.name: TestConsistencyMaps (iterated TransferDiagram)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given lists powermap1, fusionmap, powermap2 such that each triple entry is a valid TransferDiagram argument, TestConsistencyMaps repeatedly applies TransferDiagram to these arguments for all i until no more changes occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a list fusimp is specified then only those diagrams with elements of fusimp as preimages of fusionmap are considered. When an inconsistency is detected, TestConsistencyMaps immediately returns false; otherwise true is returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indeterminateness
rubrics_metrics.description: For a parametrized map paramap, Indeterminateness returns the number of maps contained in paramap, i.e., the product of lengths of lists in paramap denoting lists of several images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to measure ambiguity/branching in parametrized maps; examples show Indeterminateness([1,[2,3],[4,5],...]) = 20.

rubrics_metrics.name: PrintAmbiguity output
rubrics_metrics.description: For each map in list, PrintAmbiguity prints its position in list, the indeterminateness of the composition with paramap, and the list of positions where a list of images occurs in this composition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful diagnostic for locating ambiguous components (positions where lists occur) and their contribution to overall indeterminateness.

rubrics_metrics.name: ContainedSpecialVectors selection conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: For tbl (ordinary character table), chars (list of class functions), paracharacter (parametrized class function), and func(tbl, chars, vec) returning true/false: ContainedSpecialVectors returns all vec in paracharacter that have integral norm, integral scalar product with the principal character of tbl, and satisfy func(tbl, chars, vec)=true.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two special cases of func are IntScalarProducts (check scalar products are integers) and NonnegIntScalarProducts (check scalar products are nonnegative integers). ContainedPossibleVirtualCharacters and ContainedPossibleCharacters provide these special cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: IntScalarProducts (as func for ContainedSpecialVectors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Function that checks whether scalar products in tbl between vec and all lists in chars are integers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pass as func to ContainedSpecialVectors to filter vectors with integral scalar products; used in examples to restrict candidates.

rubrics_metrics.name: NonnegIntScalarProducts (as func for ContainedSpecialVectors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Function that checks whether scalar products in tbl between vec and all lists in chars are nonnegative integers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to restrict paracharacter elements to genuine characters (nonnegative scalar products).

rubrics_metrics.name: ContainedPossibleVirtualCharacters / ContainedPossibleCharacters
rubrics_metrics.description: Convenience wrappers providing the IntScalarProducts / NonnegIntScalarProducts special cases of ContainedSpecialVectors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as the 'contained' argument in higher-level algorithms to enumerate candidate characters or virtual characters compatible with given data.

rubrics_metrics.name: CollapsedMat behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: CollapsedMat(mat, maps) returns a record with components fusion and mat where fusion collapses those columns of mat that are equal in mat and also for all maps in the list maps; mat is the image of original mat under that fusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a canonical collapse of repeated columns taking into account auxiliary maps; examples show how last.mat indexed by last.fusion reconstructs original.

rubrics_metrics.name: ContainedDecomposables lattice membership
rubrics_metrics.description: Given constituents (list of rational class functions), moduls (list of positive integers), parachar (parametrized rational class function), and func(χ) boolean: ContainedDecomposables returns the set of all χ ∈ parachar that satisfy func(χ)=true and that lie in the Z-lattice spanned by constituents modulo moduls (i.e., spanned by constituents and {moduls[i] * e_i}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application: constituents = rational characters, moduls = centralizer orders; func typically checks nonnegative integral scalar products; note result entries are not necessarily linear combinations of constituents and may not be characters of tbl.

rubrics_metrics.name: ContainedCharacters special-case
rubrics_metrics.description: Special case of ContainedDecomposables that computes only those vectors that are characters (i.e., pass NonnegIntScalarProducts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convenience wrapper for restricting lattice points to actual characters; examples show returned lists of character vectors.

rubrics_metrics.name: InitPowerMap first approximation
rubrics_metrics.description: InitPowerMap(tbl, prime) returns a parametrized map that is a first approximation of the prime-th power map of tbl, using the conditions 1. and 2. listed in PossiblePowerMaps (73.1.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there are classes for which no images are possible according to these criteria, then fail is returned. Examples show typical initial approximations with lists of possible images.

rubrics_metrics.name: Congruences refinement (PossiblePowerMaps condition 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Congruences(tbl, chars, approxmap, prime, quick) replaces entries of approxmap by improved values according to condition 3 in PossiblePowerMaps (73.1.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each class for which no images are possible according to the tests, the new value is an empty list. Congruences returns true if no inconsistencies (empty lists) occur, and false otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: ConsiderKernels refinement (PossiblePowerMaps condition 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: ConsiderKernels(tbl, chars, approxmap, prime, quick) replaces entries of approxmap by improved values according to condition 4 in PossiblePowerMaps (73.1.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks compatibility of kernel orders of characters with group order; returns true if checks pass, false otherwise. Example shows init updated after ConsiderKernels.

rubrics_metrics.name: ConsiderSmallerPowerMaps refinement (PossiblePowerMaps condition 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: ConsiderSmallerPowerMaps(tbl, approxmap, prime, quick) replaces entries of approxmap by improved values according to condition 5 in PossiblePowerMaps (73.1.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns true if each class admits at least one image after the checks; if OrdersClassRepresentatives are not stored for tbl then true is returned without tests. quick=true restricts which classes are considered (only those with more than one possible image in approxmap).

rubrics_metrics.name: MinusCharacter definition
rubrics_metrics.description: MinusCharacter(character, primepowermap, prime) returns the parametrized map of values of χ^{p−}, defined by χ^{p−}(g) = (χ(g)^p − χ(g^p))/p, given a class function χ and an approximation primepowermap of the p-th power map.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used inside symmetrization-based power-map refinement algorithms; examples show parametrized outputs with possible sets of values.

rubrics_metrics.name: PowerMapsAllowedBySymmetrizations strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: PowerMapsAllowedBySymmetrizations(tbl, subchars, chars, approxmap, prime, parameters) replaces entries of approxmap according to condition 6 in PossiblePowerMaps (73.1.2), using symmetrizations of characters and thresholds in parameters (maxlen, minamb, maxamb, quick, contained).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure: compute minus = MinusCharacter(χ,approxmap,prime) for each χ ∈ chars; if Indeterminateness(minus)=1 and quick=false then check scalar products of minus with subchars are nonnegative integers (failure yields empty list); else if Indeterminateness(minus) < minamb then drop χ; if between minamb and maxamb compute poss := parameters.contained(tbl, subchars, minus) and Parametrized(poss) and update approxmap via UpdateMap. If no immediate improvements, branch: either union over characters with ≤ maxlen symmetrizations or pick a class C with differing possible symmetrizations and recursively union over fixes for C. Typical contained functions: ContainedPossibleCharacters.

rubrics_metrics.name: InitFusion initial class-fusion approximation
rubrics_metrics.description: InitFusion(subtbl, tbl) returns a parametrized map that is a first approximation of the class fusion from subtbl to tbl, using condition 1 in PossibleClassFusions (73.3.6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there are classes for which no images are possible according to this criterion then fail is returned. Example outputs show lists of possible images for each class of subtbl.

rubrics_metrics.name: CheckPermChar refinement for class fusions (PossibleClassFusions condition 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: CheckPermChar(subtbl, tbl, approxmap, permchar) replaces entries of parametrized map approxmap by improved values according to condition 3 in PossibleClassFusions (73.3.6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CheckPermChar returns true if no inconsistency occurred, and false otherwise. Example demonstrates its use with a permutation character and updated fusion map.

rubrics_metrics.name: ConsiderTableAutomorphisms canonicalization
rubrics_metrics.description: ConsiderTableAutomorphisms(approxmap, grp) replaces entries of approxmap by improved values according to condition 4 of PossibleClassFusions and afterwards ensures exactly one representative of fusion maps (contained in approxmap) in each orbit under the action of permutation group grp is contained in the modified parametrized map.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The function returns the list of positions where approxmap was changed.

rubrics_metrics.name: FusionsAllowedByRestrictions strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: FusionsAllowedByRestrictions(subtbl, tbl, subchars, chars, approxmap, parameters) replaces entries of approxmap according to condition 5 in PossibleClassFusions (73.3.6), using restrictions of characters and parameters (maxlen, minamb, maxamb, quick, contained) and optional components testdec, powermaps, subpowermaps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure mirrors PowerMapsAllowedBySymmetrizations: for each χ ∈ chars compute restricted := CompositionMaps(χ, approxmap); if Indeterminateness(restricted)=1 and quick=false then check scalar products of restricted with subchars are nonnegative integers (failure -> empty list); else if Indeterminateness(restricted) < minamb then drop χ; if between minamb and maxamb compute poss := parameters.contained(subtbl, subchars, restricted) and Parametrized(poss) and improve approxmap using UpdateMap. If no immediate improvements, branch similarly by enumerating possibilities up to maxlen or selecting a class C to fix and recursing. Defaults: testdec=NonnegIntScalarProducts, powermaps=ComputedPowerMaps, subpowermaps=ComputedPowerMaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: FusionsAllowedByRestrictions parameter defaults and effects
rubrics_metrics.description: parameters record must contain maxlen, minamb, maxamb, quick, contained. Optional testdec, powermaps, subpowermaps default to sensible choices (NonnegIntScalarProducts and ComputedPowerMaps).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These settings control branching limits (maxlen), ambiguity thresholds (minamb,maxamb), quick mode behavior, and which containment test to use when enumerating candidate restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unknown constructor semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: Unknown([n]) when called without argument returns a new unknown value (first one larger than all existing in session). Called with positive integer n returns the n-th unknown, creating it if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unknowns are parametrized by positive integers. When printed to files they become fixed Unknown(n) calls, so reading files across sessions may clash if unknown numbering differs. LargestUnknown global tracks largest n used.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsUnknown category and comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: IsUnknown(obj) is the category predicate for unknowns. Unknowns can be compared via = and < with all cyclotomics and certain GAP objects: Unknown(n) >= Unknown(m) iff n >= m; unknowns are larger than all cyclotomics that are not unknowns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples demonstrate comparisons like Unknown() > 3 being true and comparisons with roots of unity sometimes false; treat unknowns as new cyclotomic-like symbols ordered by their index.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arithmetical operations with unknowns
rubrics_metrics.description: The usual arithmetic +, -, *, / are defined for unknowns and cyclotomics; results are new unknowns except in specified cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiplication with zero yields zero; multiplication with one or addition of zero yields the old unknown. Division by an unknown causes an error (unknown might be zero). Unknowns behave as cyclotomics so dense lists of unknowns are row vectors and can be used in matrix arithmetic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alpha attribute (character degrees and derived length)
rubrics_metrics.description: Alpha(G) returns a list whose i-th entry is the maximal derived length of groups G/ker(χ) for χ ∈ Irr(G) with χ(1) at most the i-th irreducible degree of G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to assess derived lengths associated to irreducible degrees; used with Delta to examine degree gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delta attribute
rubrics_metrics.description: Delta(G) returns [1, al_p[2] − al_p[1], ..., al_p[n] − al_p[n−1]] where al_p = Alpha(G).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives successive differences of Alpha to highlight jumps in derived length across degrees.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsBergerCondition
rubrics_metrics.description: IsBergerCondition(chi) or IsBergerCondition(G): returns true if for chi (or all irreducible characters of G) the inequality M' ≤ ker(χ) holds for every normal subgroup M of G with M ≤ ker(ψ) for all ψ ∈ Irr(G) with ψ(1) < χ(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For groups of odd order the result is always true (Berger theorem). If false, InfoMonomial provides a degree for which the inequality is violated.

rubrics_metrics.name: TestHomogeneous output contract
rubrics_metrics.description: TestHomogeneous(chi,N) returns record with components: isHomogeneous (true/false), comment (string explaining reason), character (irreducible constituent of restriction, bound only if restriction had to be checked), multiplicity (multiplicity of character in restriction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: N may be a normal subgroup or list of class positions. Use to determine if restriction of chi to N is a multiple of an irreducible character.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsPrimitiveCharacter limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: IsPrimitiveCharacter(chi) returns true if chi is not induced from any proper subgroup, and false otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Currently only works for characters of soluble (solvable) groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: TestQuasiPrimitive contract
rubrics_metrics.description: TestQuasiPrimitive(chi) returns a record with at least components isQuasiPrimitive (true/false) and comment (reason). If chi is not quasiprimitive an additional component character is an irreducible constituent of a nonhomogeneous restriction of chi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IsQuasiPrimitive returns the boolean. Note: for solvable groups quasiprimitivity equals primitivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: TestInducedFromNormalSubgroup contract
rubrics_metrics.description: TestInducedFromNormalSubgroup(chi[,N]) returns a record with components isInduced (true/false) and comment (reason). If true, there's a component character containing a character of a maximal normal subgroup from which chi is induced. If N provided, checks only induction from that normal subgroup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IsInducedFromNormalSubgroup returns boolean. Example outputs show when a character is induced and from which component.

rubrics_metrics.name: TestMonomial outputs and usage
rubrics_metrics.description: TestMonomial(chi) or TestMonomial(G) (and variants with uselattice) returns a record containing information about monomiality. If TestMonomial proves chi monomial then result contains isMonomial (true), comment (reason), and if necessary a component character giving the linear character from which chi is induced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TestMonomial is intended to provide more diagnostic information than a simple true/false (e.g., reason strings and constructed linear characters). Use with care to reuse computed group objects/character tables to avoid repeated expensive computations.
